question: Should internal runtime continuations remain persisted as user-role transcript messages with private provenance, or should the active runtime path represent them as a non-user/internal transcript event before memory export?
rationale: This is a canonical-attribution and session-state boundary with related open security/session reports; the mechanical export filter is clear, but the durable transcript representation requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Use an internal transcript representation
options.body: Recommended: make the active runtime path persist runtime continuations as explicitly internal/non-user events, then keep memory export filtering as defense in depth.

options.title: Retain user role with provenance
options.body: Keep the current storage shape only if maintainers explicitly accept the canonical user-role record and require complete metadata-preservation and projection safeguards.

recommendation.title: Use an internal transcript representation
recommendation.body: Recommended: make the active runtime path persist runtime continuations as explicitly internal/non-user events, then keep memory export filtering as defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely available routing candidate from the supplied review timeline for the core runtime/session-boundary choice.
